title: Sensex Adds 308 Points as Nifty Reclaims 23,000 in Second Straight Rally
excerpt: Two-day Sensex gains top 1,200 points as IT and pharma lead, Trent jumps 5.2% on earnings, and October snaps a two-month losing streak — even as midcaps and smallcaps fall.
body:
• The Sensex closed 308.49 points higher at 74,459.53 and the Nifty rose 116.35 points to 23,053.10 on Friday, a second straight gain that takes the two-day Sensex advance past 1,200 points.
  • IT and pharma stocks led the rally: the Nifty IT index rose 2.3% and Nifty Pharma 1.8%, while midcap and smallcap indices fell 0.8% and 1.8%.
  • Trent jumped 5.20% after reporting a 25% rise in quarterly net profit to Rs 468 crore; Infosys, InterGlobe Aviation and Tech Mahindra were also among the top gainers.
  • For NRI investors, October closed in positive territory after two losing months — the rupee also firmed 33 paise to 94.93 per dollar on Friday.

Indian equity benchmarks extended their rally for a second consecutive session on Friday, October 30, with the Nifty 50 reclaiming the 23,000 mark as buying in information technology and pharmaceutical stocks offset weakness across the broader market. The 30-share BSE Sensex advanced 308.49 points, or 0.42%, to close at 74,459.53, after touching an intraday high of 74,742.59, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's market coverage. The NSE Nifty 50 gained 116.35 points, or 0.51%, to settle at 23,053.10.

Combined with Thursday's 905.01-point surge to 74,151.04, the Sensex has added more than 1,200 points in two sessions. The Nifty, which ended Thursday at 22,936.75, has risen nearly 2% over the week.

IT and Earnings Did the Heavy Lifting

Technology stocks were the day's strongest performers as global investors reassessed crowded artificial intelligence trades, improving sentiment toward Indian IT exporters. The Nifty IT index climbed 2.3% and the Nifty Pharma index gained 1.8%. Among individual stocks, Trent was the standout: the Tata Group retailer's shares jumped 5.20% after it reported a 25% year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit to Rs 468 crore for the September quarter, with revenue growth and operating leverage supporting earnings, PTI reported via The Daily Jagran. InterGlobe Aviation, Infosys, NTPC, Power Grid, Eternal, Tech Mahindra and HCL Technologies were also among the major gainers.

A Rally Narrower Than the Headlines

The advance was concentrated in large caps. The Nifty Midcap index fell about 0.8% and the Nifty Smallcap index dropped about 1.8%, and 11 of the 15 sector gauges compiled by the NSE ended lower, led by a 1.8% fall in consumer durables. Analysts noted the Nifty closed above the 22,800 level and reclaimed its 20-day moving average, with a breakout above 23,250 needed to confirm the next leg. October as a whole was kinder: the benchmarks snapped a two-month losing streak during the month, supported by resilient corporate earnings and expectations of a possible review of long-term capital gains taxation, according to HDFC Sky's closing report.

What It Means for Diaspora Investors

For NRIs holding Indian equities through NRE/NRO demat accounts, Friday's session paired equity gains with a firmer currency: the rupee rose 33 paise to close at 94.93 against the US dollar. The offsetting risk sits in energy — Brent crude jumped 2.17% to $117.4 a barrel, a level that historically pressures India's import bill and the rupee if it holds.

What to Watch Next

Traders will watch whether the Nifty can clear 23,250, how the remaining September-quarter earnings land, and whether Brent crude sustains above $115. A rally carried by a handful of heavyweights, with midcaps and smallcaps falling, needs broader participation to hold.
